items.title: John Pope Interview, 1959-05-01
items.q: Frank Jackson, he played with me. He played with you? He played with me. Is he still living? In my orchestra.

ctx.x: A friend of ours in New Orleans, Bill Matthews, a trombone player, has his own band. And he told us a few names to look up. One man, he didn't remember his last name. He said, Charlie, a trumpet player, had a pressing shop on Davis Avenue down near town. What kind of shop? He's not pressing, press closed. That's Charlie. That's Charlie. That's Charlie. Yes, he's dead. And I couldn't look at him. Yes, he made it. And another man he mentioned to see was Frank Jackson, a band.

Frank Jackson, he played with me. He played with you? He played with me. Is he still living? In my orchestra. Yes, but he's living in South Carolina somewhere. Oh, he's not here then. Yeah, Mobile. Yes. Very good. And I don't know of anyone else now that's around that could give me any information.
I was going to ask if you ever played on wagons when you, over in New Orleans, they advertised on wagons.
